Subject: ACME - RAG eval next steps & recommended models

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + recommended next steps so we can scope a short proof-of-evaluation for ACME: 

What we heard
- Primary use case: internal knowledge base + product docs for support assistant (short answers, code snippets).
- Target latency requirement: P95 < 400ms for conversational queries.
- Quality threshold: grounding rate > 92% on user-facing responses; minimize hallucination on product/integration docs.

Our recommended baseline for the eval (fast path)
- Retriever: dense embeddings (Redwood hosted embeddings, 1536-d) with Faiss IVF-PQ; fallback to BM25 for low-signal docs.
- Candidate retrieval: k=30 (to rerank) -> reranker top-5 for response generation.
- Reranker: cross-encoder (T5-large fine-tuned on ACME-like QA pair conversions) — expected best precision@5.
- Generator models: open-llama-7b-q4 for lower-cost baseline; Llama2-13b/Redwood-13B-quant for higher quality.

Metrics we propose to track during the eval
- Grounding rate (percentage of answers with a verifiable source link)
- Precision@k (P@1, P@5) on labeled QA set
- Hallucination/factuality errors (annotated sample)
- Latency P95 and cost-per-query estimates

Attachments / links
- Prompt set (representative prompts/queries): acme_prompt_set.csv (attached)
- RAG evaluation plan & sample eval rubric: redwood_rag_eval_plan.pdf (attached)
- Shared drive with benchmarks and previous evals: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-rag-eval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2027-001

Next steps
1) If you approve the scope above, please share a ~1-5k document sample (or a shared location) and confirm whether API keys / S3 access can be provided for indexing.
2) Technical 30-min session: Vivek (cc'd) to review retrieval & reranker choices and confirm compute footprint. Proposed slots: Thu 5/6 10:00-10:30am PT or Fri 5/7 9:00-9:30am PT.
3) We'll provision a sandbox eval (hosted) and deliver an initial eval report within 5 business days of receiving sample docs.

One ask: for the reranker recommendation we'll want 200-500 labeled QA pairs if possible (can be lightweight). If you don't have labels we can run a warm-start with heuristics and then jointly label a seed set.

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Hi Jordan / Marissa — adding a few technical details ahead of the call:

Retrieval & embeddings- Use Redwood hosted embeddings (1536-d) for dense retrieval. For a 5k-doc collection we recommend Faiss IVF-PQ with an nlist tuned to your corpus (~256) and PQ bits tuned to balance recall vs index size. For production we can move to HNSW for lower-latency KNN.
- Retrieval k: start with k=30; this provides good recall for reranker to work on. If you have long documents, consider chunking at ~512 tokens with overlap 50 tokens.

Reranker recommendation- Cross-encoder (T5-large or similar) fine-tuned on ACME QA pairs will give the best grounding precision. Operational approach: run cheap bi-encoder vector similarity for candidate generation and cross-encoder on top 100 -> pick top 5 for generator.
- If compute is constrained, we can use a lightweight monoBERT reranker for top-50 -> top-5.

Generator model guidance- Start with open-llama-7b-q4 as a cost-effective baseline. If you see quality regressions on product docs, promote to Llama2-13b-quant or Redwood-13B. We'll provide prompt templates and guardrails.

Evaluation plan notes- Proposed eval: run retrieval+rerank+generation across the provided prompt set (attached) and compute P@1, P@5, grounding rate, hallucination/error rate on a labeled sample (200 queries). We'll also run a small latency sweep to measure P95.
- Cost/time: for 5k docs & 2k eval queries the sandbox run should complete within 48 hours once data is indexed; estimated compute spend (infra + model cost) ~USD 2.5k-4k depending on model choices. We'll refine after seeing doc sizes.

I've attached a small reranker config we use for tuning: reranker-config.yaml (attached).

I'll be on the 5/6 10:00am PT slot — see you then.
